meta.title: Canopy — 2026 reforestation impact study
meta.description: Research readout of Canopy's five-year reforestation study across 9 sites and 412 plots: native mixes versus plantations, stream cooling, crew effects, limits and a $4.2M recommendation.

slides.heading: Native forest stands grew back 64% more canopy than plantations.
slides.lead: Five years, 18,000 acres, nine partner sites.
slides.notes: Lead with the number. The trustees decide the 2027 budget at the end of this session.

slides.heading: Three findings change where the next $4.2M should go

cards.title: Native mixes win
cards.body: 64% more canopy cover than single-species plots by year five.

cards.title: Shade cools streams
cards.body: Restored catchments ran 2.1°C cooler in August.

slides.notes: If time runs short, these three cards are the whole study.

slides.heading: We tested whether cheap single-species planting is a false saving
slides.body: Plantations cost $1,900 per acre, native mixes $2,600. Most funders pick the cheaper option and count trees planted, not canopy that survives.
slides.aside: If native mixes return more canopy per dollar, our planting rule should change in 2027.

slides.heading: We measured 412 plots on nine sites over five years

stats.label: Partner sites, 18,000 acres in three basins
Plots surveyed by drone and on foot

slides.heading: Nine sites span the Sauk, Skagit and Nooksack river basins
slides.lead: Each site paired native and single-species plots on the same slope.

slides.heading: Native mixes reached 59% canopy cover by year five, plantations 36%
slides.lead: Source: drone canopy survey, 412 plots, 2021–2026. 59% vs 36% is 64% more cover.

slides.quote: The mixed plots shaded the creek by year three. The pine rows never did.
slides.by: Lena Ortiz · Crew lead, Upper Sauk site

slides.heading: Streams in restored catchments ran 2.1°C cooler in August
Sites led by local crews kept 91% of saplings alive
slides.lead: Five-year sapling survival by who ran the site. Source: ground counts, 412 plots.

slides.heading: We expected budget to decide survival; crew tenure did instead
slides.left:
Higher spend per acre, higher survival.
Irrigation would matter most.
slides.right:
Spend explained little once crews were stable.
Crews with 3+ years lost a third as many saplings.
slides.notes: This is the finding trustees will question. The crew data is not randomised; say so before they ask.

slides.heading: How sure we are, and what we would change
slides.lead: Confidence first, then three ranked moves.

slides.heading: Our evidence is strong on canopy and weakest on birds
Put the 2027 budget into native mixes run by local crews
slides.lead: Ranked by canopy gained per dollar. Total $4.2M.

items.label: Plant only native mixes on new sites
Fund 6 local crew leads for 3 years

slides.notes: Ask for the vote on all three together; they depend on each other.

slides.heading: Fund native forests and local crews with the 2027 $4.2M
slides.lead: Approve today and planting starts on the Sauk site in March.
